summary.text: Misery and painful distress personified, born fatherless from Nyx beside Momus.
Hyginus lists Miseria among the children of Night and Erebus together.

story.text: Murky Night bore painful Oizys without union with any father. Hesiod places Misery immediately after Momus, making suffering itself a member of the ancient household of Night.
In Hyginus' Latin genealogy, Miseria is not fatherless: she belongs to the long brood produced by Nox and Erebus.
